---------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m4p2t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Hospitals, TotalUnits, MaxQueue

VARIABLES storage, reserved, issued, queue

vars == <<storage, reserved, issued, queue>>

Init ==
    /\ storage = TotalUnits
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ issued = 0
    /\ queue = << >>

Request(h) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, h)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storage, reserved, issued>>

Reserve ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ storage > 0
    /\ storage' = storage - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED issued

Issue ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<storage, queue>>

Return ==
    /\ issued > 0
    /\ issued' = issued - 1
    /\ storage' = storage + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reserved, queue>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hospitals : Request(h)
    \/ Reserve
    \/ Issue
    \/ Return

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

UnitConservation == storage + reserved + issued = TotalUnits
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Hospitals = {h1, h2}
    TotalUnits = 3
    MaxQueue = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnitConservation
nl:
A regional blood bank tracks a fixed pool of blood units as they move through
its fulfillment pipeline. Every unit is always in exactly one of three places:
resting in cold storage, reserved against an accepted hospital request, or
already issued for delivery. Hospitals submit requests, which land in a bounded
intake queue; when the queue is full the bank applies backpressure and refuses
new requests until earlier ones drain. A worker pulls the oldest queued request
and reserves one unit from storage for it, then later issues that reserved unit
to the courier. Occasionally an issued unit comes back unused and returns to
storage. A hospital may be slow to submit follow-up requests, leaving its
request sitting in the queue, but no unit is ever conjured up or thrown away:
the pipeline only relocates units among the three places.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of units in storage, reserved, and issued always sums to the fixed total the bank started with, so no blood unit is ever created or destroyed.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m9p5t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES ctrlEpoch, net, applied, firings

vars == <<ctrlEpoch, net, applied, firings>>

Msg == [dst: Machines, ep: 1..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
    /\ ctrlEpoch = 0
    /\ net = {}
    /\ applied = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ firings = {}

BumpEpoch ==
    /\ ctrlEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ ctrlEpoch' = ctrlEpoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<net, applied, firings>>

Emit(m) ==
    /\ ctrlEpoch > 0
    /\ [dst |-> m, ep |-> ctrlEpoch] \notin net
    /\ net' = net \cup {[dst |-> m, ep |-> ctrlEpoch]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, applied, firings>>

Deliver(msg) ==
    /\ msg \in net
    /\ net' = net \ {msg}
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![msg.dst] =
                     IF msg.ep > applied[msg.dst] THEN msg.ep ELSE applied[msg.dst]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, firings>>

Fire(m) ==
    /\ firings = {}
    /\ applied[m] > 0
    /\ firings' = {[machine |-> m, ep |-> applied[m]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ctrlEpoch, net, applied>>

Next ==
    \/ BumpEpoch
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Emit(m)
    \/ \E msg \in Msg : Deliver(msg)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Fire(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AtMostOneFiring == \A f, g \in firings : f = g
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {a, b}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneFiring
nl:
A network of vending machines is coordinated by a central controller that
periodically bumps a global configuration epoch and emits epoch-stamped
reconfiguration messages to individual machines. The channel does not preserve
order: emitted messages sit in a shared pool and may be delivered to their
target machine in any sequence, and a machine only adopts an epoch newer than
the one it currently holds, ignoring stale arrivals. At some point the operator
triggers a one-time promotional lockdown: a single machine, using whatever epoch
it has adopted, fires the lockdown and records which machine fired and at which
epoch. This lockdown is irreversible and must happen at most once across the
whole network, even though reordered messages could tempt a second machine to
fire late. The recorded firing is therefore unique.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The promotional lockdown fires at most once, so any two recorded firings must be one and the same firing.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m9p4t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Players, Lobbies, Capacity, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES assign, epoch, roundOpen, crashed

vars == <<assign, epoch, roundOpen, crashed>>

Occupants(l) == {p \in Players : assign[p] = l}

Init ==
    /\ assign = [p \in Players |-> "none"]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ roundOpen = FALSE
    /\ crashed = {}

StartRound ==
    /\ roundOpen = FALSE
    /\ epoch' = (epoch % MaxEpoch) + 1
    /\ roundOpen' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, crashed>>

CloseRound ==
    /\ roundOpen = TRUE
    /\ roundOpen' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assign, epoch, crashed>>

Join(p, l) ==
    /\ roundOpen = TRUE
    /\ assign[p] = "none"
    /\ Cardinality(Occupants(l)) < Capacity
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![p] = l]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roundOpen, crashed>>

Crash(p) ==
    /\ assign[p] \in Lobbies
    /\ assign' = [assign EXCEPT ![p] = "crashed"]
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roundOpen>>

Next ==
    \/ StartRound
    \/ CloseRound
    \/ \E p \in Players, l \in Lobbies : Join(p, l)
    \/ \E p \in Players : Crash(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected ==
    \A l \in Lobbies : Cardinality(Occupants(l)) <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Players = {p1, p2, p3}
    Lobbies = {x, y}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A matchmaking service places players into game lobbies over successive
configuration rounds, each identified by an incrementing epoch. The service
starts a round, which opens the current epoch for joins; while a round is open,
an unplaced player may join any lobby that still has a free seat, and each lobby
seats a fixed maximum number of players. The service can close the current round
to stop accepting joins before starting the next epoch. Any placed player may
crash silently at any moment, vanishing from its lobby without notifying the
service and thereby freeing a seat. Because seats are strictly limited, the
service must never let a lobby hold more players than its seat capacity, no
matter how joins, crashes, and round changes interleave.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every lobby always holds at most its fixed seat capacity of active players, so bounded capacity is never exceeded.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m1p0t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANT N

Nodes == 0 .. (N - 1)
Succ(n) == (n + 1) % N

VARIABLES holder, mode, requests, completed

vars == <<holder, mode, requests, completed>>

Init ==
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ mode = [n \in Nodes |-> "idle"]
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ completed = {}

Request(n) ==
    /\ n \notin requests
    /\ n \notin completed
    /\ mode[n] = "idle"
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, mode, completed>>

Pass(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ mode[n] = "idle"
    /\ n \notin requests
    /\ holder' = Succ(n)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<mode, requests, completed>>

Enter(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ mode[n] = "idle"
    /\ n \in requests
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![n] = "critical"]
    /\ requests' = requests \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, completed>>

Exit(n) ==
    /\ mode[n] = "critical"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![n] = "idle"]
    /\ completed' = completed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, requests>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Request(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Pass(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Enter(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Exit(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion ==
    \A m, n \in Nodes :
        (mode[m] = "critical" /\ mode[n] = "critical") => m = n
=============================================================================

CONSTANT N = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A matchmaking service arranges its worker nodes in a logical ring and circulates
a single access token around it to guard one shared arbitration slot, which only
one node may occupy at a time. Nodes raise interest by posting requests; these
requests accumulate in an unordered pool, so the service may honor them in any
sequence, not in the order they arrived. A node holding the token that has no
pending request of its own simply forwards the token to its ring successor. When
the token holder does have a pending request, it enters the arbitration slot,
does its work, and later exits, after which it is marked done for this cycle.
Because only the current token holder may ever enter the slot and there is
exactly one token, two different nodes must never occupy the arbitration slot
simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one node is ever in the critical arbitration slot at the same time, so any two nodes seen in the slot must actually be the same node.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m6p4t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Robots, Capacity, LeaseDur, MaxTime

VARIABLES clock, lease, requests, grants

vars == <<clock, lease, requests, grants>>

ActiveLeases == {r \in Robots : lease[r] > clock}

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ lease = [r \in Robots |-> 0]
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ grants = {}

Request(r) ==
    /\ lease[r] = 0
    /\ r \notin requests
    /\ r \notin grants
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease, grants>>

IssueGrant(r) ==
    /\ r \in requests
    /\ Cardinality(ActiveLeases) + Cardinality(grants) < Capacity
    /\ requests' = requests \ {r}
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, lease>>

ApplyGrant(r) ==
    /\ r \in grants
    /\ grants' = grants \ {r}
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, requests>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTime
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, requests, grants>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ lease[r] > 0
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, requests, grants>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Request(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : IssueGrant(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : ApplyGrant(r)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Release(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityNeverExceeded == Cardinality(ActiveLeases) <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2, r3}
    Capacity = 2
    LeaseDur = 2
    MaxTime = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
A fleet of warehouse robots shares a limited bank of charging couplers whose
total simultaneous capacity is fixed. A robot that needs power posts a request;
requests collect in an unordered pool. The controller reserves a coupler by
issuing a grant, but grants travel asynchronously and are applied by the robots
in any order, not necessarily the order issued. When a robot applies its grant
it takes a lease stamped with an expiry time; once the global clock passes that
expiry the lease silently lapses and its coupler capacity is freed without any
message. A robot may also release its lease early. To stay within the fixed
electrical budget, the controller reserves capacity at grant-issue time so that
no matter which order the outstanding grants are applied, the number of live
leases can never exceed the total coupler capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of live (unexpired, unreleased) charging leases never exceeds the fixed coupler capacity.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m8p4t3 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Clients, Capacity

VARIABLES coarseOwner, fineOwner, spool, waiting

vars == <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, spool, waiting>>

Init ==
    /\ coarseOwner = "none"
    /\ fineOwner = "none"
    /\ spool = 0
    /\ waiting = {}

Request(c) ==
    /\ c \notin waiting
    /\ coarseOwner # c
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, spool>>

AcquireCoarse(c) ==
    /\ c \in waiting
    /\ coarseOwner = "none"
    /\ coarseOwner' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fineOwner, spool, waiting>>

AcquireFine(c) ==
    /\ coarseOwner = c
    /\ fineOwner = "none"
    /\ fineOwner' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, spool, waiting>>

Spool(c) ==
    /\ fineOwner = c
    /\ spool < Capacity
    /\ spool' = spool + 1
    /\ coarseOwner' = "none"
    /\ fineOwner' = "none"
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}

Drain ==
    /\ spool > 0
    /\ spool' = spool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarseOwner, fineOwner, waiting>>

GiveUp(c) ==
    /\ coarseOwner = c
    /\ coarseOwner' = "none"
    /\ fineOwner' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, waiting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : AcquireCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : AcquireFine(c)
    \/ \E c \in Clients : Spool(c)
    \/ Drain
    \/ \E c \in Clients : GiveUp(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SpoolWithinCapacity == spool <= Capacity
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Clients = {c1, c2}
    Capacity = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SpoolWithinCapacity
nl:
A print shop runs a shared spooler that buffers at most a fixed number of jobs.
To submit a job a client must acquire two nested locks in order: first the coarse
printer lock, then the fine spool-slot lock; the fine lock can only be taken by
whoever already holds the coarse lock. Clients first register interest, then work
through the lock hierarchy, and finally deposit their job into the spool and drop
both locks at once. The physical printer drains the spool one job at a time. A
client may be slow: it can hold the coarse lock for a while and then give up,
releasing both locks without ever spooling, but it never fails outright and stays
eligible to retry. However many clients contend and however slowly they proceed,
the spooler must never buffer more jobs than its fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of jobs buffered in the spool never exceeds the spooler's fixed capacity.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m9p5t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, permit, runState, finalEpoch, crashed

vars == <<epoch, permit, runState, finalEpoch, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ permit = "available"
    /\ runState = "open"
    /\ finalEpoch = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ runState = "open"
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, runState, finalEpoch, crashed>>

Crash(w) ==
    /\ w \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, permit, runState, finalEpoch>>

Recover(w) ==
    /\ w \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, permit, runState, finalEpoch>>

Finalize ==
    /\ permit = "available"
    /\ runState = "open"
    /\ permit' = "used"
    /\ runState' = "finalized"
    /\ finalEpoch' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Crash(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Recover(w)
    \/ Finalize

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FinalizeConsistent ==
    /\ (runState = "finalized") <=> (permit = "used")
    /\ (runState = "finalized") => (finalEpoch = epoch)
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    MaxEpoch = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FinalizeConsistent
nl:
A print shop processes a large print run that is reconfigured over numbered
epochs while it stays open; a controller may bump the epoch only before the run
is finalized. Several workers assemble the run, and any worker may crash silently
and later recover, without affecting the run's committed state. Finalizing the
run is an irreversible, one-time action gated by a single-use finalize permit:
the finalize consumes the permit, marks the run finalized, and stamps the epoch
at which it happened. Once finalized, the run can never be reopened and the epoch
can never be bumped again, so the stamped finalize epoch stays equal to the
current epoch forever after. The single-use permit guarantees the finalize fires
at most once no matter how workers crash and recover.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The run is marked finalized exactly when the single-use permit has been consumed, and once finalized its stamped epoch equals the current epoch, so the irreversible finalize can have happened at most once.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m4p0t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Aircraft, MaxQueue

VARIABLES mode, queue

vars == <<mode, queue>>

NoneOnRunway == \A a \in Aircraft : mode[a] # "onRunway"

Init ==
    /\ mode = [a \in Aircraft |-> "ground"]
    /\ queue = << >>

Request(a) ==
    /\ mode[a] = "ground"
    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, a)

Grant ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ NoneOnRunway
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "onRunway"]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

Clear(a) ==
    /\ mode[a] = "onRunway"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "ground"]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Crash(a) ==
    /\ mode[a] \in {"queued", "onRunway"}
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "crashed"]
    /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA x : x # a)

Reset(a) ==
    /\ mode[a] = "crashed"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "ground"]
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Request(a)
    \/ Grant
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Clear(a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Crash(a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Reset(a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RunwayMutualExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Aircraft :
        (mode[a] = "onRunway" /\ mode[b] = "onRunway") => a = b
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {a1, a2}
    MaxQueue = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RunwayMutualExclusion
nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates a single active runway among inbound
aircraft. Aircraft on the ground request departure and are appended to a bounded
takeoff queue; when the queue is full the controller applies backpressure and
refuses further requests until it drains. The runway is a critical resource that
exactly one aircraft may occupy at a time: the controller grants the runway to
the aircraft at the head of the queue only while the runway is free, the aircraft
takes off and later clears the runway. An aircraft that is queued or on the
runway may crash silently, vanishing from the system and (if it was queued)
being spliced out of the queue; a crashed aircraft can later be reset back to the
ground. No matter how requests, grants, crashes, and resets interleave, two
aircraft must never be on the runway at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one aircraft occupies the runway at any time, so any two aircraft on the runway must be the same aircraft.

    /\ Len(queue) < MaxQueue
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]

    /\ Len(priorityQueue) < MaxPrio
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "queued"]
    /\ priorityQueue' = Append(priorityQueue, a)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, takeoffs>>

GrantPriority ==
    /\ Len(priorityQueue) > 0
    /\ NoneOnRunway
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![Head(priorityQueue)] = "onRunway"]
    /\ priorityQueue' = Tail(priorityQueue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, takeoffs>>

    /\ Len(priorityQueue) = 0
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ NoneOnRunway
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![Head(queue)] = "onRunway"]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)

    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "ground"]

    /\ queue' = SelectSeq(queue, LAMBDA x : x # a)
    /\ priorityQueue' = SelectSeq(priorityQueue, LAMBDA x : x # a)
    /\ UNCHANGED takeoffs

Reset(a) ==
    /\ mode[a] = "crashed"
    /\ mode' = [mode EXCEPT ![a] = "ground"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, priorityQueue, takeoffs>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : RequestNormal(a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : DeclareEmergency(a)
    \/ GrantPriority
    \/ GrantNormal
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Clear(a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Crash(a)
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Reset(a)

RunwayMutualExclusion ==
    \A a, b \in Aircraft :
        (mode[a] = "onRunway" /\ mode[b] = "onRunway") => a = b

CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {a1, a2}
    MaxQueue = 2
    MaxPrio = 1
    MaxTakeoffs = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RunwayMutualExclusion
nl:
An air-traffic control system allocates a single active runway among inbound
aircraft using two bounded takeoff queues: an ordinary queue and a shorter
priority queue for emergencies. A grounded aircraft either files an ordinary
request, appended to the ordinary queue, or declares an emergency, appended to
the priority queue; when a queue is full the controller applies backpressure and
refuses further entries there. The runway is a critical resource that exactly one
aircraft may occupy at a time: the controller grants it only while the runway is
free, always draining the priority queue before the ordinary one, and the granted
aircraft takes off and later clears the runway, bumping a bounded takeoff tally.
A queued or airborne aircraft may crash silently, vanishing and being spliced out
of whichever queue held it; a crashed aircraft can later be reset to the ground.
However requests, grants, crashes, and resets interleave, two aircraft must never
occupy the runway at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one aircraft occupies the runway at any time, so any two aircraft on the runway must be the same aircraft.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od15m1p2t0 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS N, Total

Traders == 0 .. (N - 1)
Succ(t) == (t + 1) % N

VARIABLES holder, inv, pool, crashed

vars == <<holder, inv, pool, crashed>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_)
SumOver(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET t == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN inv[t] + SumOver(S \ {t})

Init ==
    /\ holder = 0
    /\ inv = [t \in Traders |-> IF t = 0 THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ pool = 0
    /\ crashed = {}

PassToken(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ holder' = Succ(t)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inv, pool, crashed>>

Deposit(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ inv[t] > 0
    /\ inv' = [inv EXCEPT ![t] = inv[t] - 1]
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Withdraw(t) ==
    /\ holder = t
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ inv' = [inv EXCEPT ![t] = inv[t] + 1]
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, crashed>>

Crash(t) ==
    /\ t \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, inv, pool>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Traders : PassToken(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Deposit(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Withdraw(t)
    \/ \E t \in Traders : Crash(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

UnitsConserved == SumOver(Traders) + pool = Total
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    N = 3
    Total = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT UnitsConserved
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction for a single security whose total number
of tradable units is fixed. Traders sit in a logical ring and pass a single
access token around it; only the current token holder may touch the auction, so
access to the matching engine is exclusive. While holding the token, a trader may
deposit one of its own units into the central auction escrow, or withdraw one
unit from the escrow into its own inventory, thereby reallocating ownership. A
trader may crash silently at any time: it stops depositing and withdrawing, and
its holdings simply freeze in place, but the token can still advance past it
around the ring so the auction never stalls. Because deposits and withdrawals
only move existing units between trader inventories and the escrow, the total
number of units in the whole system never changes.

    \/ \E i \in Instances, r \in Runways : Operate(i, r)

Two independent control-tower instances share one common pool of runways. To use
a runway a tower must first acquire a time-limited lease on it, stamped with an
expiry equal to the current clock plus a fixed duration; a runway can be leased

operating is exclusive per runway. A tower finishes operating, and may release a

    /\ finalized = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]
    /\ claimed = [i \in Instances |-> 0]

    /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, claimed, seats>>

    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<finalized, claimed, seats>>

    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![i] = Demand]

when an instance has no leader one can be elected, and a sitting leader can fail
at any time, leaving that instance leaderless until re-election. The irreversible
action is publishing an instance's final roster: only its current leader may do
it, it can happen at most once per instance (guarded by a one-shot finalized
flag), and it draws that instance's fixed seat demand from the shared pool. The
system tracks how many seats each instance has claimed. Because a roster is
published at most once and each publication claims exactly the instance's demand,
the shared pool always equals the initial number of seats minus the total seats
claimed by the instances.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Each instance has claimed exactly its demand if finalized and zero otherwise, and the shared seat pool always equals the initial seats minus the total claimed, so each irreversible roster publication happened at most once.

    ELSE LET t == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE

    /\ txState = [t \in Txns |-> "init"]
    /\ votes = [t \in Txns |-> {}]
    /\ record = 0
    /\ capacity = 0

    /\ txState[t] \in {"init", "prepared"}
    /\ p \notin votes[t]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![t] = votes[t] \cup {p}]
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "prepared"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, capacity>>

Commit(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] = "prepared"
    /\ votes[t] = Participants
    /\ record + t <= capacity
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "committed"]
    /\ record' = record + t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, capacity>>

Abort(t) ==
    /\ txState[t] \in {"init", "prepared"}
    /\ txState' = [txState EXCEPT ![t] = "aborted"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, record, capacity>>

Grow ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txState, votes, record>>

Shrink ==
    /\ capacity > 0
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<txState, votes, record>>

    Participants = {p1, p2}
    MaxCap = 3
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A vending machine network maintains one shared accumulator record and applies
updates to it through two-phase commit. Each update transaction carries a
distinct weight. In the prepare phase every participant machine votes for a
transaction; once all participants have prepared it, the coordinator may commit
it, which atomically adds that transaction's weight to the shared record. A
prepared or fresh transaction may instead be aborted, contributing nothing. The
number of units the record may hold is a runtime capacity that can grow or shrink
at any time, and a transaction can commit only if the record would stay within
the current capacity. Because each committed transaction contributes its weight
exactly once and commits are atomic, the shared record always equals the exact
sum of the weights of all committed transactions: no committed update is ever
lost or overwritten.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared record always equals the sum of the weights of exactly the committed transactions, so no committed update to the shared record is ever lost.

--------------------------- MODULE W4Od7m5p0t1 ---------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Arbiters, Quorum, MaxEntries

VARIABLES votedFor, inCritical, requests, entries

vars == <<votedFor, inCritical, requests, entries>>

Votes(c) == Cardinality({a \in Arbiters : votedFor[a] = c})

Init ==
    /\ votedFor = [a \in Arbiters |-> "none"]
    /\ inCritical = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ entries = 0

Request(c, a) ==
    /\ inCritical[c] = FALSE
    /\ [crn |-> c, arb |-> a] \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {[crn |-> c, arb |-> a]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votedFor, inCritical, entries>>

Grant(c, a) ==
    /\ [crn |-> c, arb |-> a] \in requests
    /\ votedFor[a] = "none"
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![a] = c]
    /\ requests' = requests \ {[crn |-> c, arb |-> a]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCritical, entries>>

Revoke(a) ==
    /\ votedFor[a] # "none"
    /\ inCritical[votedFor[a]] = FALSE
    /\ votedFor' = [votedFor EXCEPT ![a] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCritical, requests, entries>>

Enter(c) ==
    /\ Votes(c) >= Quorum
    /\ inCritical[c] = FALSE
    /\ inCritical' = [inCritical EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
    /\ entries' = IF entries < MaxEntries THEN entries + 1 ELSE entries
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votedFor, requests>>

Exit(c) ==
    /\ inCritical[c] = TRUE
    /\ inCritical' = [inCritical EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
    /\ votedFor' = [a \in Arbiters |-> IF votedFor[a] = c THEN "none" ELSE votedFor[a]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requests, entries>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, a \in Arbiters : Request(c, a)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, a \in Arbiters : Grant(c, a)
    \/ \E a \in Arbiters : Revoke(a)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Enter(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Exit(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

LaneMutualExclusion ==
    \A c1, c2 \in Cranes :
        (inCritical[c1] /\ inCritical[c2]) => c1 = c2
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {c1, c2}
    Arbiters = {a1, a2, a3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxEntries = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT LaneMutualExclusion
nl:
A container-ship crane yard guards one shared critical travel lane that only a
single crane may occupy at a time. To enter the lane a crane must win a quorum
(a majority) of the yard's arbiters. A crane sends vote-request messages to
arbiters; these requests sit in an unordered pool and are answered in any order,
so grants may be reordered. Each arbiter grants its single vote to at most one
crane at a time. A crane that has collected a quorum of votes may enter the
critical lane; on leaving it releases all the votes it held. An arbiter may
revoke and re-cast its vote, but only while the crane it voted for has not yet
entered the lane. Because any two majority quorums share an arbiter and an
arbiter votes for only one crane, two cranes can never both hold a quorum while
in the lane, so two cranes are never in the critical lane at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one crane occupies the critical lane at any time, so any two cranes in the lane must be the same crane.

AcqFine(i) ==

    /\ coarse = i
    /\ fine = "free"
    /\ fine' = i
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "f"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, total, pool, stage>>

    /\ fine = i
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![i] = pool]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "read"]

    InitialPool = 2
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
Two independent matchmaking instances share one common pool of match credits and
move credits, one at a time, into a shared accumulated-matches record. Every
transfer is a read-modify-write protected by two nested locks acquired in order:
first a coarse pool lock, then a fine record lock (which only the coarse-lock
holder may take). Holding both locks, an instance reads the current pool value
into a private staging slot, then commits by writing the pool back decremented by
one and adding one to the accumulated record, finally dropping both locks. An
instance may instead release its locks at any point and back out without
committing. Because the lock hierarchy serializes transfers, an instance's staged
read is never stale at commit time, so every credit removed from the pool is
added to the record and none is lost. The total credits in the pool plus the
accumulated record therefore stays constant.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared pool plus the accumulated-matches record always equals the initial number of credits, so no credit update is ever lost.

nl:

settlement funds and post batches against a shared ledger guarded by optimistic
locking. The ledger carries a version number. To post, an instance first reads
the current version into its private cache. It then attempts to commit, which
succeeds only if its cached version still equals the ledger's current version
(the optimistic check): a successful commit bumps the version, draws one unit from

current one, and every authorized commit draws exactly one unit from the pool, so
the pool plus the version count stays equal to the initial funds.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, intake, routed>>

    /\ leader' = "none"

    /\ load[b] < Cap

    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![b] = load[b] + 1]
    /\ routed' = IF routed < MaxRouted THEN routed + 1 ELSE routed
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term>>

    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![b] = load[b] - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, intake, routed>>

bounded intake buffer onto a set of conveyor belts, each with a fixed load
capacity. Leadership uses failover: when there is no leader a node can be elected

step-downs, arrivals, routes, and drains interleave, no belt ever holds more bags
than its fixed capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every conveyor belt always holds at most its fixed load capacity of bags, so bounded capacity is never exceeded.
